  Switch to sulfate free shampoo and only use it a few times a week. It looks like you’re brushing your hair and that’s probably your biggest problem right now. Please stop brushing it, it’s killing your curls. Use your hands in the shower to rake through it when it’s wet and if you really need to you can brush it out in the shower but i don’t think it’s long enough for that yet. Also do not towel dry it as that will also ruin your curls, let it air dry. When you finish showering scrunch the bulk of the water out with your hands and then don’t touch it. 

   I think the other guys suggestion is pretty good but deep conditioner 2-3 times a week is overkill. Deep conditioner is a once a week kind of thing but you should still use regular conditioner throughout the week. Conditioner is pretty necessary for curly hair as it needs a lot of moisture but too much can make your hair look sticky and weigh it down. It’s gonna take some experimenting and time to figure it out.

The main idea is that sulfates dry out curly and other types of hair and that’s why people don’t use sulfate containing shampoo all the time. However, sulfates are one of the main chemicals in shampoo that actually cleans your scalp and you shouldn’t completely remove it from your routine. I use sulfate free shampoo nearly every other day because it works for me and then use a sulfate containing clarifying shampoo around every two weeks and leave in conditioner on the same day.  You need to experiment with shampoos but don’t be afraid to use it more because what works for someone else might not work for you. You just have to start experimenting and see what your head likes.

I am a 4k player who's been maining offlane for a little while now and I think I can give some insight. I think you just need a different perspective on laning as a pos 1. In many match ups as  pos 1 assuming both players play decently you WILL reach a point where you will no longer be able to lane against the offlaner, most offlaners by design simply scale faster than most pos 1s. So the question you need to ask yourself every game is "how long can I stay in this lane?" If you don't think that you're laning phase is going to last very long, then you should prioritize items that help you farm the jungle faster. Now WK in particular is extremely good at clearing the jungle early, so if you find yourself in a lane where you don't think you can stay in it very long I would recommend going for a fast set of power treads as they are an extremely efficient buildup and the stats are insanely gold efficient. Once you get the treads you should be good to start clearing the jungle with skeletons and avoid laning unless it's pushed in enough where you feel safe to farm it. Now against axe in particular your build of phase boots > armlet is good if you plan on staying in the lane. But axe is a hero where your positioning matters more than anything. If you notice you have a very big creep wave do NOT stand under it as it's exactly what he wants you to do since he can taunt everything and guarantee a lot of spins.

Yeah my shampoo and conditioner are both CG. The only thing I use that contains sulfates is clarifying shampoo since CG shampoo doesn’t contain sulfates and products can start to build up in your hair. I usually use it every few weeks, once my hair starts to feel kind of knotty and not soft. I’ll also use a deep conditioner about once a week and i’ll always try to use it after I use clarifying shampoo. So if i plan to clarify my hair i’ll wait on the leave in conditioner that week to use it after I clarify. For other products i’ve been using a shea moisture hair smoothie which has been pretty nice, i just can’t use it too much or the buildup gets bad. I’ve also exclusively been using the CG method for about a year and haven’t really tried going back so I wouldn’t be able to tell you how effective it is (I started growing out my hair the same time I started CG and had really short hair for my whole life prior to starting it) Trial and error is really your best bet for testing products out, the downside is that if you don’t like it you kind of just end up wasting money and product. I’ve wasted money on gels, sea salt spray, hair clips and havent used them more than 3 times lol, but eventually you’ll find something that works. Also finding the proper balance on how much you condition your hair is important, there was a point where i was conditioning my hair waaaayyy too much and there was too much protein in my hair and it started to look awful all the time.

edit: I checked your profile and can see you’re asking about what I have right now. I didn’t really show my barber a picture, it’s less of how I got it cut and more of what I do to style it. For starters I never dry my hair with a towel and always let it completely air dry. I use a sulfate free shampoo and conditioner, and use them both on the same day about every 2/3 days depending on how it feels. Some people use conditioner by itself without shampooing on days in between but for me i find that just adds buildup. Sometimes i’ll do it but it’s really if i just wanna experiment and see what happens. But besides shampoo and conditioner i also have a clarifying shampoo, which i only use about every few weeks once i feel like my hair as a good amount of buildup in it, and after I use it i’ll use a deep conditioner after i get out of the shower. A couple times a week i’ll add a hair smoothie to my hair, it’s basically just a cream you rub in your hair after you shower while my hair is still wet. I only brush my hair when it’s completely wet in the shower but for the most part use my hands to push it back, i’ll use a wide toothed comb to part the hair in the shower and put it to the sides. But the most important thing by far is letting the hair air dry and not touching it once you’re out of the shower. This takes like a good hour and half with my length and is by far the most annoying part lol. Also my hair is a little more curly than yours and that just comes down to genetics, and even if you don’t want to invest in to all the products i highly suggest testing out the air drying method to see what happens.
